newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - July 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - July 23.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories Wednesday:
* Boeing indicated it is willing to alter or drop its use of exclusive aircraft supply contracts, as a move to appease the European Commission on the company's plan to merge with McDonnell Douglas.
* Stocks soared to record levels after Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan said there is no imminent threat of a rise in interest rates.
* Qatar is sitting on not only a vast oil supply but a natural gass supply believed to be the largest reservoir in the world.
* The Time Warner Cable system has agred to carry Rupert Murdoch's 24-hour Fox news channel in New York City.
* Philip Morris reported a 13.3 percent earnings rise.
* Bell Atlantic, NYNEX, and Northern Telecom reported unexpectedly high earnings growth.
* Drug makers SmithKline Beecham, Warner-Lambert and Schering-Plough reported strong profits.
* Texaco and Amoco reported profits that surpassed forecasts.
* Disney said its earnings rose 18 percent in the latest quarter.
* IBM 's chief shuffled the company's management ranks.
* In agreeing to buy Oppenheimer Holdings for $525 million in cash, Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce is stepping toward its goal of building a worldwide securities businiess.
* The parent of United Airlines said earnings before charges rose 12 percent.
* The Chinese economy grew at a world-leading 9.5 percent in the first half of the year.
